parsed.rationale: Although `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` and `AudioPlayerProtocol` share several member names (`installRenderTap:()`, `removeRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, `play`, `stop:()`), the overlap is not deep enough to justify a parent protocol. Key members diverge in type and semantics: `eventStream` carries `AsyncStream<AudioPlayerEvent>` in one protocol but `AsyncStream<AudioPlayerInternalEvent>` in the other; `play` is `() throws` in `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` but `()` in `AudioPlayerProtocol`; `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` exposes `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, and `volume` (engine-level concerns) while `AudioPlayerProtocol` exposes `state:PlayerState` and `stateStream:AsyncStream<PlayerState>` (higher-level state-machine concerns). The structural evidence confirms `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, indicating the pipeline itself found no strongly shared fields. Extracting a common parent would require either weakening the type signatures or leaving so few members in the parent that it provides no useful abstraction.
